text: Across March 30–April 12, sleep increased abruptly and remained longer on all 14 nights: 448 versus 328 minutes in the preceding 28-day baseline (+120 minutes, 36%; range 442–457). Sleep began around 23:12 instead of 01:12, while waking stayed at 07:00. Weekdays and weekends showed the same shift, with only slight further lengthening (~0.5 minute/day) and no return to baseline. Steps averaged 7,963 versus 8,044 but trended downward (~25/day); weekend steps fell from 8,195 to 7,784 while weekday averages remained similar. Active time stayed near 55 minutes, beginning at 21:00. Low movement remained near 450 minutes in ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Resting heart rate (56.1 versus 56.0 bpm) and RMSSD (45.1 versus 45.5 ms) stayed similar despite longer sleep. Activity duration had little association with next-wake-date sleep in 13 aligned pairs (r=0.07). All metrics were complete.

text: Steps dropped at the start of March 30–April 12 and remained below the preceding 28-day baseline on every observed day: 6,433 versus 9,552 daily (−3,119; −33%), ranging 6,262–6,675 without recovery. Weekday/weekend means were 6,404/6,500 versus 9,517/9,640. April 7 daytime metrics were missing because wear was only 360 minutes, so continuity across that day is uncertain. Active time changed little (53.5 versus 55.1 minutes), remaining continuous bouts starting at 21:00; steps and active minutes were essentially unrelated within the window. Low movement stayed near baseline (451 versus 448 minutes), in ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Sleep remained 470 versus 469.5 minutes, around 22:50–07:00, with no meaningful weekday/weekend difference. Resting heart rate and RMSSD stayed close to baseline (56.3 versus 56.1 bpm; 45.5 versus 45.2 ms). Activity versus next-wake-date sleep had a modest negative association (r=−0.32; 12 pairs).

text: Steps and active minutes fell abruptly on March 30 and remained reduced throughout April 12, across weekdays and weekends, without recovery. Compared with the preceding 28-day baseline, steps averaged 2,321 versus 7,998 (71% lower), with every day at 2,086–2,500; active time averaged 4.9 versus 55.2 minutes (91% lower), ranging 0–10. March 30 and April 8 recorded zero active minutes with no activity interval; other days had one 21:00 bout lasting 2–10 minutes, versus baseline continuous 50–60-minute bouts. All metrics were present with 720 daytime wear minutes daily. Low movement stayed similar (447.5 versus 450.5 minutes), comprising ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Sleep remained near baseline (469.4 versus 470.5 minutes), with starts 22:42–22:58 and waking at 07:00; it fluctuated but trended slightly longer. Resting heart rate stayed 55–57 bpm (56.3 versus 56.1); RMSSD averaged 44.8 versus 45.3 ms and trended upward. Thus the movement reduction accompanied little change elsewhere

text: Across March 30–April 12, steps abruptly fell from the 28-day baseline mean of 7,998 to 2,321/day (−71%), and active minutes from 55.2 to 4.9/day (−91%). Both stayed low throughout all 14 days, including weekends, without recovery; recorded activity at 21:00 shortened from 50–60 to 0–10 minutes. Low movement remained similar: 447.5 versus 450.5 minutes/day, in ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps, rather than one continuous interval. Sleep also remained stable at 469.4 versus 470.5 minutes, with starts at 22:42–22:58 and waking consistently at 07:00; weekday/weekend differences were small. Resting heart rate averaged 56.3 versus 56.1 bpm and RMSSD 44.8 versus 45.3 ms, staying within baseline ranges. Their daily association became moderately inverse (r=−0.59); activity versus next-wake-date sleep was weak (r=0.32, 13 pairs), and steps versus active minutes was negligible. No metrics were missing, with consistent wear coverage.

text: During March 30–April 12, steps and active minutes fell abruptly and remained below the preceding 28-day baseline throughout weekdays and weekends, without recovery. Steps averaged 2,321 versus 7,998 (−71%); active minutes averaged 4.9 versus 55.2 (−91%), ranging 0–10 daily. The usual continuous 21:00 bouts shortened to 2–10 minutes when present; March 30 and April 8 recorded zero. Sleep remained near baseline: 469 versus 471 minutes, starts around 22:51, and waking consistently at 07:00. Low movement also stayed similar (448 versus 451 minutes), in ten daytime intervals with five-minute gaps. Sleep starts stayed near 22:50 with 07:00 waking and little weekday/weekend difference. Activity remained one 21:00 bout; daytime low movement comprised ten roughly 44–46-minute bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Activity duration had little association with sleep ending the following day (r=0.10). All metrics were complete.
